summary: The Longer Catechism, a standard Russian Orthodox statement of the faith, teaches that faith and good works are inseparable, since faith without works is dead. On predestination it says that God has predestined to give all men, and has actually given them, preparatory grace and means sufficient for happiness. Citing the exposition of the Eastern patriarchs, it says that God foresaw that some would use their free will well and others ill, and predestined the former to glory while condemning the latter. The questions read do not say how a person is made right with God in the terms used in the Western debates over justification, or whether believers can fall away.

points.question: How do faith and works relate?
points.answer: A right faith in God and a life according to faith, with good works, go together; the catechism says a life according to faith and good works must be inseparable from faith because faith without works is dead.

points.question: Did God choose who would be saved?
points.answer: God's predestination of man to happiness remains unchanged; God has predestined to give all men preparatory grace and sufficient means. Citing the Eastern patriarchs, it says God foresaw who would use free will well or ill, and predestined the former to glory and condemned the latter.

review.note: Questions 4-5 and 120-125 read in the azbyka.ru English text on 2026-11-12. The catechism's longer treatment of faith, hope and the means of grace was not read, so justification and perseverance are left "not stated" rather than guessed. Not yet checked by a second reviewer.
